scenario.symptoms: A user edited a shared note on phone and laptop while offline for a flight. After reconnect, one device’s paragraph vanished with no warning.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Sync uses last-write-wins by client timestamp without clock sync or merge semantics. The server picked the laptop edit because its clock was ahead.

incident.headline: Last-write-wins with skewed client clocks silently drops offline edits

agenda.goal: Merge concurrent offline edits without silent data loss.
agenda.opener: Two offline edits to the same note—one disappeared. How should conflict resolution work?

evidence.strong: CRDT or operational transform, version vectors, server-assigned revision ids, and UI conflict surfacing.
evidence.adequate: Field-level merge for plain text but whole-document LWW otherwise.

misconceptions.pattern: Trusting client wall clocks for ordering.
misconceptions.challenge: Laptop clock ahead of phone—who wins and is that fair?

probes: How does the user recover text that lost a merge?
What metadata travels with each edit?
hints: CRDTs merge without a single winner.
agenda.referenceFix: Use CRDT/OT with version vectors, reject whole-document LWW, store edit history, and show merge UI when concurrent branches diverge.

scenario.symptoms: Users deleted tasks while offline, but items popped back after syncing from an older tablet that still held the rows locally.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Deletes are implemented as hard deletes locally without tombstones propagated to the server. Slow devices replay stale snapshots that reinsert rows.

incident.headline: Missing tombstones let stale clients resurrect deleted objects

agenda.goal: Ensure deletes win over stale replicas during sync.
agenda.opener: Deleted tasks came back from an old device—what sync metadata prevents resurrection?

evidence.strong: Tombstone records with deletion vector, retention window, and merge rules that prefer delete over stale upserts.
evidence.adequate: Server-side delete flag without propagating tombstones to all clients.
evidence.weak: Hard delete locally with no server tombstone.

probes: What happens if two devices delete and update the same id?
hints: Deletes are events, not absence of rows.
GC tombstones only after all clients caught up.
agenda.referenceFix: Persist tombstones with deletion timestamps/vectors, replicate them to clients, reject upserts that predate tombstones, and GC after sync horizon.

scenario.symptoms: After a week offline, the app froze on ‘Syncing…’ and consumed 400 MB in minutes. Users on cellular complained about data caps.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Catch-up pulls the full change log since epoch for every collection instead of incremental cursors or paginated deltas.

incident.headline: Catch-up replays entire history instead of incremental deltas

agenda.goal: Efficiently catch up long-offline clients without huge transfers.
agenda.opener: A user offline for a week triggered a massive sync—how should catch-up be designed?

evidence.strong: Per-device sync tokens, paginated delta feeds, compression, Wi-Fi preference, and snapshot+bootstrap for very stale clients.
evidence.adequate: Incremental since last sync but unbounded page size.
evidence.weak: Full table dump on every reconnect.

probes: When do you snapshot vs stream deltas?
How do you resume a interrupted catch-up?
hints: Store last applied sequence id on device.
agenda.referenceFix: Track per-client vector/sequence cursors, page deltas with backoff on cellular, offer snapshot bootstrap when lag exceeds threshold, and resume with range requests.
